skill.title: Real estate document review checks
skill.summary: A real estate review procedure for leases, estoppels, rent rolls, title and encumbrance materials, and transaction documents, with explicit checks for premises, figures, dates, consents, source completeness, cross-document conflicts, and final deliverable consistency.
instructions: Inventory property, lease, title, survey, estoppel, rent roll, and transaction documents, and identify the controlling instrument for each issue.
Confirm each source was read through its complete text, including continuations or truncated sections, before relying on it; record missing portions as open items.

Build a cross-source conflict matrix for every material property metric, date, party, and obligation that appears in more than one instrument, listing each occurrence, source, controlling basis, and resolution or unresolved status.
Verify legal descriptions, premises, unit or area figures, allocations, and measurement bases against source schedules and independent arithmetic, and preserve the calculation trail.
Reconcile lease abstracts, rent rolls, estoppels, and underlying leases for parties, term, rent, escalations, options, and encumbrances.
Check title and encumbrance items against transaction requirements and identify required consents, releases, subordination, or estoppel documents.
Compute date-dependent obligations and prorations independently, and flag ambiguities in commencement, expiration, notice, or closing timing.
After drafting, render and inspect the final deliverable to confirm required sections, tables, definitions, cross-references, and figures match the verified issue log and conflict matrix.
Confirm that every property-level conclusion is tied to a specific document and that missing, inconsistent, or unverified items are expressly flagged.
triggers: Lease, estoppel, rent roll, title, survey, or purchase agreement review
Real estate due diligence and closing checklist preparation
Real estate source sets with overlapping or conflicting property figures
exclusions: Standalone land-use or zoning policy research
Property marketing material review without source documents
